explanation: Its tongue pins each catch against spines on the roof of its mouth while it fishes for more. After the breeding season it sheds the bright outer plates of its bill.

claims.text: Atlantic puffins can carry several small fish crosswise in their bills at once.
Northern gannets, great cormorants and herring gulls do not carry rows of fish crosswise in their bills.
A puffin holds fish against backward-pointing spines on its palate with its tongue.
Atlantic puffins shed the colourful outer plates of their bills after the breeding season.
